sections.html:
Giles County lies in Virginia's southwest corner against the West Virginia line, with Pearisburg as the seat. Four towns have their own governments: Narrows, Pearisburg, Pembroke and Rich Creek. Glen Lyn dissolved as a town in 2024 and now counts as unincorporated. Eggleston and Ripplemead are named places on the census map, along with small settlements such as Newport, Staffordsville, Kimballton, Maybrook and White Gate.

Headcount has slipped for more than a decade. The county has 8,285 housing units, and the 2020 census found 14.2% of them empty. Among occupied homes, 73.7% belong to the people living in them.

Fewer buyers per listing usually means a house sits longer, especially an older one or one on a back road. Describe the lane or road honestly, since a gravel drive changes how quickly an inspector or contractor can reach the property.

The state legislature built Giles in 1806 out of pieces of Montgomery, Monroe, Wythe and Tazewell. That origin shows up in paperwork, where an old deed might name a parent county or a road that has since been renamed. If you inherited acreage described in very old language, the Giles County Circuit Court clerk keeps the land records that trace ownership back, and asking to see them early prevents a snag near closing.

Older masonry chimneys deserve a look too. A strong earthquake centered here on May 31, 1897 damaged chimneys near its center, and an inspector of an old house may still check the flue and the stonework.

The Commissioner of the Revenue holds the assessment records and hears appeals, while the Treasurer sends and collects the bills. Both are elected.

An online real estate data portal run for the county displays 2026 reassessment values and owners as of January 1, 2026. Anything changed later in the year stays off the bill now being issued, which is built on that January 1, 2026 snapshot. Finish a new roof or an addition after that date and, as a rule, this year's amount stays put.

Questions go to the Commissioner of the Revenue's office at (540) 921-3321, whose records are the authoritative ones for any parcel you research.

  • Verify the parcel number, acreage and building description on the portal ahead of listing day.
  • Find out from the Commissioner whether a land use program or relief application is on file for the property.
  • Request from the Treasurer a payoff figure with penalty and interest included.

Giles refreshed its values for 2026, and the new numbers drive the bill you receive. If the figure looks off, compare the portal's acreage, building description and ownership with what you know about the house. A wrong square footage or an outbuilding that was torn down years ago is a factual error, and factual errors are the easiest to fix with the Commissioner's office. Photographs, a survey or a copy of a closing statement from your own purchase can settle the question in one visit. Resolve it before listing, because a buyer's lender will look at the same record you do.

Installment dates are printed on your bill, and the Treasurer's office will confirm them by phone, including any extension that a reassessment year brings. With the bill in front of you the answer takes seconds, so locate it before you contact anyone. If you have sold or are about to, ask whether the next installment has already been billed.

Your first conversation belongs with the Commissioner of the Revenue, whose office set the value. State law gives a person assessed by a commissioner a window to ask for a correction: three years after the tax year ends, or one year after the assessment date, whichever falls later. On real estate the statute covers mistakes the commissioner made and factual errors that came out of a general reassessment.

Boards of equalization exist for the period after a general reassessment, and the circuit court generally sits above them. A dispute about value alone travels that path. Build a folder first with recent comparable sales, photographs of problems and repair bids, because every step rests on evidence.

Virginia ranks the real estate tax lien above all others, and it lasts until the taxing authority has its money. A purchaser at a sale, or a foreclosure trustee, must steer proceeds toward the taxes assessed on the parcel, a term that takes in penalty and interest. At an ordinary closing, the settlement agent asks the Treasurer what is owed and deducts it from the seller's proceeds. How the current year splits between buyer and seller is left to the contract, so write down who carries which months.

  1. Copy the parcel number off the portal record.
  2. Phone the Treasurer for the balance, with penalty and interest counted in.
  3. Pass the number along to the title company.
  4. After the closing, check that the lien shows as released.

sections.h2: Selling a Giles County house that needs work
sections.html:
Typical sellers here inherit homes in towns like Narrows and Pearisburg, hold older houses on large rural parcels, or carry repairs they have put off. With 14.2% of units empty in 2020, an unoccupied house is a common sight here, and insurance, utilities and tax all continue while it waits for a buyer.

Selling for cash removes the showings and the repair list. Cash Home Buyers takes houses in their current condition, and the title company settles unpaid real estate tax out of what you receive at closing. Compare any offer against your numbers by lining up the tax payoff, the names on the deed and the portal record first. Then you can see what remains once the lien is gone, and whether that beats paying for a roof or foundation fix and waiting on the market.

sections.h2: What to bring to a call with the county
sections.html:
Staff move faster when you open the call with details in hand: the parcel number, every name on the deed and your most recent bill. When an owner has died, mention it immediately. Whoever acts for the estate must show documented authority before anyone can sign a deed or release a payoff. A tenant in the house is worth mentioning as well, since it changes showings and timing.

Wherever you can, get the answers on paper. A Treasurer's payoff, a parcel summary from the Commissioner and a note about land use or relief status hand the title company what it needs and leave little to chance during the final week.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Giles County real estate assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Commissioner of the Revenue at (540) 921-3321. The county's real estate portal treats that office's records as the authoritative ones.

faqs.q: Does a repair I make this year change my Giles County bill?
faqs.a: Generally not for the current bill. Value changes made during the year do not show on current billing, which rests on January 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Is a Giles County tax lien ahead of my mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 58.1-3340 of the Code of Virginia puts the real estate tax lien ahead of any other lien or encumbrance until the taxing authority is paid.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Giles County house that owes back tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, with penalty and interest, comes out of the sale proceeds at closing, so ask the Treasurer for a written payoff before the closing date.

faqs.q: How long do I have to ask the Commissioner for a correction?
faqs.a: Three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the assessment date, whichever is later. For real estate it covers errors by the commissioner or factual errors in a reassessment.
